candidates.source_summary: A Rochdale-born entrepreneur has been recognised as a finalist at the Rochdale Business Awards after developing a UK-wide directory that helps businesses and travellers find licensed chauffeur and private hire operators.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Rochdale-born entrepreneur whose UK-wide directory helps businesses and travellers identify licensed chauffeur and executive private hire operators has been recognised as a finalist in the Rochdale Business Awards. John Byrne, Co-Founder of Rochdale-based Junction 21 Chauffeurs , was named one of three finalists in the Business Person of the Year category at the Rochdale Business Awards, held on 13 November 2026. Born and raised in Rochdale, Byrne has spent almost two decades building Junction 21 Chauffeurs alongside his wife and business partner, Pauline. In recent years, he has also led the development of the UK Licensed Chauffeur & Executive Private Hire Operator Directory, an independent online resource designed to improve visibility and promote professional standards within the chauffeur and private hire sector. The directory was established to provide businesses, travel buyers and members of the public with a simple way to identify licensed chauffeur and executive private hire operators throughout the United Kingdom, helping users locate businesses that hold the appropriate licences issued by their local authorities. Launched in 2026, the UK Licensed Chauffeur & Executive Private Hire Operator Directory has grown to include more than 100 licensed operators from across the UK. Developed alongside Byrne’s work at Junction 21 Chauffeurs, what began as an idea in Rochdale has evolved into a national resource used by businesses and travellers across the UK, helping raise awareness of industry standards and the importance of booking through properly licensed operators. Reflecting on his finalist recognition, Byrne said: “Being named as one of the three finalists was an achievement in itself and something I am incredibly proud of. Rochdale has always been home, and to be recognised alongside other business leaders from across the borough was a genuine honour.” “The directory was created to support professionalism within the industry and provide a simple way for people to find licensed operators. It has been rewarding to see something that started in Rochdale develop into a resource that is now used by businesses and travellers throughout the UK.” In addition to being shortlisted for Business Person of the Year, Junction 21 Chauffeurs also sponsored the Business of the Year category for organisations with annual turnover exceeding £5 million, reflecting the company’s ongoing commitment to supporting enterprise and economic development across the borough.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thomson appeared at Glasgow Sheriff Court after being extradited from Dubai A man has been extradited to Scotland from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to face organised crime charges. Alan Thomson is accused of running a cross-border drug operation in Glasgow and England between March and June 2020. Thomson, 46, and co-accused Mohamed Eldirani, 55, are also alleged to have "furthered serious and organised crime" between March and June 2020. The men made no plea during an initial appearance at Glasgow Sheriff Court and were remanded in custody. Thomson was arrested in Dubai following a joint probe involving officers in the UAE and Scotland and the National Crime Agency. The offences allegedly took place in various locations across the UK, including in Robroyston in Glasgow, and Rochdale, Greater Manchester. Thomson is alleged to have directed others to sell and supply substances including cannabis, cocaine and diamorphine and to collect, store and transport criminal money.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Staff at 10 primary schools have been equipped to inspire the next generation of engineers. Last week, staff from the schools across Rochdale and Oldham took part in a CPD training day so they could the deliver the Primary Engineer Vehicle Programme in their schools. The programme allows pupils to build and test their own vehicle models while getting to interact with engineering professionals in class, as well as attending a joint school event as they celebrate their achievements at the end of the programme. The practical session gave teachers a hands-on opportunity to build their confidence in delivering STEM projects to pupils. The current academic year marks first year of partnership between Rochdale Council, Rochdale Development and Primary Engineers with the aim of inspiring Rochdale’s next generation of engineers. READ MORE: Care home plan approved despite objections The vehicle programme gives the opportunity for schools to gain access to a full package of opportunities, including a full day CPD training course, high-quality kits and classroom resources which will enable 60 pupils in each school to build 15 shoebox locomotives and 15 motorised locomotives. The schools will also receive all resources to continue the programme with new pupils in their school for the next academic year.

candidates.source_summary: Six people have been arrested in Middleton for attempting to import cannabis worth almost £6 million from Canada.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Six people have been arrested in Middleton for attempting to import cannabis worth almost £6 million from Canada. Police in Canada uncovered the plan and officers there swapped the cannabis — which was hidden with a shipment of timber — for a synthetic product. The shipment was allowed to continue its journey to the UK and was tracked, resulting in officers from Greater Manchester Police’s Serious Organised Crime Group seizing a lorry at an address in Heywood Old Road in Middleton on Wednesday night. GMP said: “Through the strong working relationship developed between our SOCG officers and Canadian law enforcement partners, we were alerted to an attempted import of approximately 590kg of cannabis, which was concealed within a large lumber shipment destined for the UK. “The drugs, worth an estimated street value of £5.9 million, had been hidden within sophisticated concealments inside the shipment. “Canadian authorities successfully seized the cannabis before it left the country, and replaced it with a synthetic substitute. “Following its arrival at docks in Liverpool, we closely monitored the container as it was transported by HGV to an address in Heywood Old Road in Middleton. “Officers maintained surveillance on the shipment and observed a number of individuals interacting with the container.

The ceremony took place on Thursday 5 November at Emirates Old Trafford and was hosted by TV personality Amy Powell. The award recognises an individual delivering clear and measurable positive impact on people and communities across Greater Manchester. Parvez founded Breaking Barriers in Rochdale in 2019. Under his leadership, the organisation has delivered over 80 projects, reached nearly 30,000 young people through Theatre in Education programmes, engaged over 200 artists and built audiences of over 100,000 through live events and 655,000 digitally. Two programmes were central to Parvez’s nomination. Crossing the Line addresses child criminal exploitation and county lines, producing a 60% increase in awareness of grooming and a 33% increase in understanding of peer pressure after a single session. Blind Side tackles violence against women and girls (VAWG), recording a 38% increase in understanding of VAWG after a single performance. Both programmes equip young people with the knowledge to recognise harmful behaviour and the confidence to speak up, take action and keep themselves and their peers safe. Parvez shared: “I am truly humbled by this recognition. To be acknowledged in my home borough, amongst so many incredible people doing such important work across Greater Manchester means everything. “My vision has always been to build an organisation that uses creativity as a tool for social change. I believe the arts have a unique power to reach people of all ages in ways that other interventions cannot, to spark conversations that change attitudes and to give communities the confidence to speak up and take action. That is what Breaking Barriers was built to do, and to be recognised for that work here in Greater Manchester is something I am incredibly proud of.” The win adds to a significant period of national recognition for Parvez and Breaking Barriers. In October 2026, the organisation won the Spark the Change Award at the National Arts and Cultural Education Awards for Crossing the Line and was a finalist for the Partnership Award at the National Children and Young People Now Awards. Breaking Barriers was also named as a finalist at the Rochdale Diversity Awards for the Cohesion Award.

Ardan Hartley appeared at Burnley Magistrates’ Court and pleaded guilty to two environmental offences. The court heard that on or around July 29, Hartley dumped controlled waste in a skip on the driveway of a private home on Newchurch Road, Stacksteads, Rossendale. The court heard the waste consisted of builders’ rubble and old bathroom furniture. A picture of the waste from Rossendale Borough Council (Image: RBC) Hartley, of Halifax Road, Rochdale, did not have the authority of a current environmental permit allowing the waste to be deposited there. Images shared by Rossendale Borough Council show a skip filled with a bath which appears to have been cut in half, a toilet, bin bags with unknown contents, nails, paint tins, and rubble from a mix of materials. He admitted an offence under the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months. An investigation into Haider Ali was launched following information received that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked in Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on January 4, 2025. Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Ali, who was travelling as a passenger, exited the vehicle and began to speedily walk away before officers detained him. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of more than £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, all of which were seized. Ali was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs and taken to custody where further searches recovered two bundles of several wraps of a brown and a white substance. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. Following this, investigators also uncovered that Ali was not only dealing drugs at street level, but he was also managing other street dealers. Evidence suggested that Ali had progressed from being a street dealer in 2014 to holding a significant role within the Adam OCG in 2024 into 2025, managing street dealers and the dedicated dealer phone, and directing those below him on where there next deal is.

Next week, the council’s Employment and Equalities Committee will consider the steps being taken to support staff after figures for 2025-26 show total number of days lost was 30,707.80, which equates to £4,237,676.40 in sick pay. This averages 11.49 days per full-time employee due to sickness absence, with the main reason being stress/depression — an 11.2% increase on the previous year’s total of 10.33 days. The latest figures show that 65% were long-term absences, 35% were short-term absences and both are consistent with figures for previous years. The report says that the council is continuing to support staff with their health and wellbeing, and is providing a programme of initiatives throughout the year. This includes prevention of ill health and promotion of staff wellbeing. Detailed analysis of the 2025/2026 figures show that the main reasons for long-term absence were stress/depression, operative/post-operative and back and sprains, strains, bruises and breaks. For short-term absences, the reasons are stress/depression, colds/flu/viral infections, diarrhoea/ vomiting/sickness bug.
candidates.source_title: Rise in council staff off with stress and depression - Rochdale Times

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands of people enjoyed Rochdale’s Ignite Fire Festival and the Christmas Lights switch-on. More than 15,000 people attended the three-day event which lead up to the festive switch-on at the town hall on Sunday. Ignite, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK and organised by Rochdale Development Agency, transformed the square and gardens around the town hall into a trail of fire, lights and entertainment. Immersive night-time trail BODY took visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience was the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite was its north-west premiere. Visitors were taken on a dramatic journey as they walked through the glowing embers of human metabolism – the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Visitors arriving at BODY, the trail enjoying its north-west premiere at Ignite Fire Festival There was also a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle and a stunning backdrop, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall. Drum Machine — the 20-strong drumming collective — brought its dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival, performing multiple sets each night.

Saturday’s 3-2 defeat to Northampton - also led by a former MK Dons assistant head coach in the form of Chris Hogg - was Dale’s fourth in a row and secured Watson his marching orders. “We would like to thank Ian for his hard work and commitment during his time at the Crown Oil Arena and wish him every success in the future,” said a club statement. “The process to appoint a successor is already underway, and the club will give a further update in due course.” In a statement later in the week, they confirmed: “A thorough recruitment process is under way, and we are speaking with a number of candidates. “We want to be clear that this is an appointment we will not rush. candidates.source_summary: Campaigners fighting to save Rochdale's College Bank flats from demolition are calling on community leaders to step in and save the landmark tower blocks
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Campaigners fighting to save Rochdale’s College Bank flats from demolition are calling on community leaders to step in and save the landmark tower blocks. Yesterday, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing announced that demolition and redevelopment of the site is the only viable option for the 61-year-old tower blocks known as the Seven Sisters. It said refurbishing them would cost at least £269 million and take up to 12 years — estimated at £388,000 for each of the 766 flats before VAT. RBH said the renovations would add another 50 years to the lifespan of the buildings, while redevelopment would provide 601 homes in a mix of sizes, creating a minimum additional 249 bedrooms, and the properties would last “significantly longer”. Reacting to the news, Greater Manchester Tenants Union said the decision was part of a “managed decline” overseen by the housing provider — a claim RBH denies. GMTU said: “Campaigners and the wider community are very disappointed with the decision to pursue demolition by RBH. “For 10 years the tenants and leaseholders of College Bank have suffered one mistaken decision after another. “RBH claims the decision is based upon ‘a detailed review of all available scenarios’ but it has only allowed for a costing of an overpriced refurbishment plan based upon installing a second staircase in each block of College Bank (under new regulations following the Grenfell disaster).”

Post-mortem examinations found cocaine and the anxiety drug pregabalin in Allister's system. Emergency services were called to Lea's home in Padiham at about 03:00 BST on 9 August 2022 after reports that Allister was not breathing. He was pronounced dead at hospital a short time later. The court heard that Lea had subjected the infant to a pattern of abuse, including an incident in which she painted a symbol in blood on the baby's head and shared images of it with friends.

candidates.source_summary: John Morris believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on Christmas Island.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: John Morris has long campaigned for a study into the health impacts of Britain's nuclear programme A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment". John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island. It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s. Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt". "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight . Burnham told campaigners in Downing Street that he would launch an independent investigation Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site.

candidates.source_summary: The Challenge Cup will enter an exciting new era in 2027, with a refreshed format, a bold new identity and a renewed ambition to make one of rugby league's most iconic competitions bigger, more compelling and more accessible to fans.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The 2027 Challenge Cup campaign will kick off on the weekend of January 16-17, bringing together clubs from across the rugby league pyramid in a format that celebrates the depth and heritage of the sport, while building towards the ultimate prize at Wembley Stadium. The first round draw will take place on Monday 30 November at Wembley Stadium, live on the newly-launched Challenge Cup YouTube channel. It will feature 28 community clubs, offering teams from across the country a chance to face the professional game's biggest names on the road to the national stadium. A brand-new identity for the Challenge Cup will be unveiled on Monday, signalling the beginning of the competition’s next chapter and providing a distinctive platform to connect with existing supporters, attract new audiences and elevate the competition's profile. The launch will also include the announcement of a new commercial partner and a dedicated ticket sales window, giving rugby league fans an exclusive opportunity to secure their place at Wembley Stadium on Saturday 5 June. Under the revised format, the bottom four Super League teams from 2026, plus newly-promoted London Broncos, will enter in the fourth round, with the remaining top-flight clubs, excluding Catalans Dragons and Toulouse Olympique (who will not participate in 2027), joining in the fifth round. The Challenge Cup will once again start in January with a full round of community club ties, before 10 Championship clubs join in the second round, the remaining 10 joining in the third round. The fourth and fifth rounds will take place in March, followed by the quarter-finals in April and the semi-finals on the weekend of May 8-9. The successful finalists will then have four weeks to prepare for the Challenge Cup Final on Saturday 5 June. The Women's Challenge Cup final will once again take centre stage at Wembley on Saturday 5 June as part of Finals Day, celebrating the continued growth and importance of the women's game. The Wheelchair Challenge Cup final will follow, on the weekend of June 26-27, ensuring the competition's revitalised chapter embraces all forms of the sport.

candidates.source_summary: The Championship is set for a new-look 2027 season, with an East and West Conference format, an expanded race for the play-offs and a fresh approach to the 1895 Cup.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Under the improved structure, clubs will play 18 league fixtures within their own conference, with nine home games and nine away games, before the top five in each conference progress to the Championship play-offs. A four-week play-off series will build towards a Grand Final scheduled for October 3, while the Shield Trophy will offer a further opportunity for clubs outside the leading places to compete for silverware. The conference model will give clubs a clear route through the regular season, with all 18 league fixtures played against opponents from their own conference. Each club will have nine opportunities to play in front of their home supporters, alongside nine away fixtures, with conference standings determining qualification for the Championship play-offs. The opening conference round is scheduled for January 21–24, with the final round of league fixtures planned for September 2–5. Week 1: The top five teams in both the East and West conferences will reach the play-offs. In week one, fourth will play fifth in each conference for a place in the next round. Week 2: In week two, the team that finished top of each conference will play the lowest-placed team still in the competition from that conference. The teams that finished second and third will also play each other within their own conference. Week 3: The winners of those games will meet in the East and West Conference Finals in week three. In each final, the team that finished higher in the league will play at home.

Colleagues and local parents nominated her for the award. Lindsay said, “It was really humbling to be shortlisted, that was enough for me, but I have absolutely loved my time in Rochdale. “Teaching the children has been an absolute joy and every experience has made me a better teacher, leader and person. “I owe a lot to Rochdale, I just loved every moment of it and to end it in this way was very special to me.” Seventeen other awards were presented at the ceremony. candidates.source_summary: Living Well Rochdale has carried out 2,000 free community health checks across Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton. The team referred 1,017 people to their GP for further assessment.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Living Well Rochdale has carried out 2,000 free community health checks across Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton. The team referred 1,017 people to their GP for further assessment. Rochdale Borough Council commissioned the programme, which launched on 31 October 2025. Living Well Rochdale’s cardiovascular disease team has held sessions at community venues, GP practices, workplaces, places of worship and cash and carry stores. The checks include blood pressure, height and weight measurements and a finger-prick blood test for blood sugar and cholesterol. Participants are also given their body mass index and a QRISK3 score, which estimates their risk of cardiovascular disease over the next 10 years. Kuiama Thompson, director of public health and communities at Rochdale Borough Council, said, “This is another milestone in a successful collaboration between the council and Living Well in tackling cardiovascular disease in our borough. “We're very proud of the innovative approach that we've developed with Living Well, which addresses health inequalities by understanding and putting the needs of our residents first. “This is a model of bringing healthcare into communities, in turn saving lives across the borough. By making those vital early interventions with these health checks we can reduce cardiovascular disease and ensure that all of our residents are given the chance they deserve to live longer and healthier lives.” Living Well Rochdale and the council’s public health team were highly commended in the Community Engagement category at the 2026 MJ Awards. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A plan that will shape the future of Rochdale has been signed off and sent to the government for approval. The borough’s Local Plan will mould how it will look and its priorities until 2039. Under the plans, around 11,000 new homes will be built and the borough’s railway stations will get a major revamp. After one final round of consultation, the hefty 175-page document has been approved by town hall chiefs. Once given the green light by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, it is expected that formal adoption of the plan will come later in 2027 or early 2028. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The main controversy of the Local Plan had been reducing the minimum threshold of affordable housing from 20 per cent to 15 pc. This was done because it was not financially viable, a town hall meeting in July was told. But the latest town hall meeting saw the cabinet put that threshold back up to 20 pc for ‘all developments of 10 dwellings or more’. Housing forms a substantial part of the plan, with the land carved out for new homes already mapped out by the Places for Everyone plan. The PfE plan is a giant housing strategy adopted by nine out of 10 Greater Manchester councils. PfE would see around 175,000 homes built across the city region over the next two decades and is expected to bring forward investment and major redevelopment in Rochdale and across the city-region. The Rochdale council is anticipating a major boost in the coming years through the Atom Valley scheme. The vision to build 7,000 new homes, create 20,000 ‘high-quality’ jobs and carve out 17m sq ft of employment land has already taken hold. But the Local Plan is focusing on Rochdale alone. The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is at the beating heart of what the local authority really wants to achieve. The concept would see the land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line reconfigured into places for people to live, work and play. These hubs would focus on the stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough and a new Slattocks station. To get the very latest Greater Manchester stories in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Combined with walking and cycling routes, park and rides, new public realms and community spaces, these hubs hope to attract more people into the area and in turn boost the local economy. Overall, the strategic plan covered a huge array of topics that would influence how the borough would grow. These areas include climate and energy, economic growth and town centres, housing, natural environment, design and place-making, healthy communities and sustainable transport. All these categories have been considered for each town and local centre across the area, which have been prioritised in order of importance to the borough’s growth ambitions.

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale say they "will not rush" their search for a new manager after parting company with Ian Watson.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale have said they "will not rush" their search for a new manager after they parted company with Ian Watson on Sunday. After their 3-2 defeat by Northampton Town, Dale's fourth league defeat in a row, the club sacked the former South Shields boss after only five months in charge. Following promotion to League Two via the play-offs in dramatic circumstances back in May, Rochdale lost manager Jimmy McNulty to Greater Manchester neighbours Stockport County. While McNulty has led Stockport to the top of League One, Rochdale have struggled in the fourth tier so far this season and currently lie 22nd in the table , just two points above the relegation zone. In a written statement on the club's website, Rochdale's board of directors acknowledged fans' "frustration" at the current situation. "A thorough recruitment process is under way, and we are speaking with a number of candidates," Rochdale's board wrote. "We want to be clear that this is an appointment we will not rush. The next permanent head coach must share our values and our vision for Rochdale AFC. "Our full focus is now on finding the right person to take the club forward and fulfil our minimum ambition of retaining our EFL status."

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A headteacher who dedicated more than 43 years to the education and wellbeing of pupils across the borough has been recognised with a lifetime achievement award. Lindsay Torrance, 65, is one of the borough’s longest-serving teachers. She received the special honour on Friday during the latest Raising Rochdale Education Awards. Awarded in recognition of the outstanding contribution she has made throughout her career, Lindsay’s commitment to teaching was celebrated in front of a packed room of fellow teachers and education professionals at Rochdale Town Hall. Lindsay first began teaching in the borough on September 1, 1983, at Marland Hill Primary School before taking on other teaching roles at Spotland and Heybrook. She was also deputy headteacher at St Edward’s Church of England (CoE) Primary School before becoming headteacher of Castleton Primary in 1998. One person described her as the “soul” of Castleton, while another described Lindsay as an “inspiration to generations of pupils, staff and the wider community”.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A three-year-old boy died after being found choking with a bowl of food at his nursery days after his birthday, a court heard today. An inquest into the tragic death of Thiago Wall was opened and adjourned by a coroner in a brief hearing on Wednesday morning at Rochdale Coroner's Court. The court heard Thiago tragically died at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital on November 5. He was taken to hospital from the Cosy Toes nursery on Mainway East, Middleton, on November 2. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter A provisional cause of death was given as 'choking on a bowl of food'. The court heard a police investigation was continuing. No arrests have been made, Greater Manchester Police said previously. Thiago had only recently turned three, with his date of birth given at the hearing as October 26, 2023. His full name was given as Thiago William Wall. Police coroner's officer, Kathy Skelton, confirmed the contents of a report to senior coroner Joanne Kearsley at the hearing. Thiago, she said, was born in Manchester. The court heard he was taken to hospital on November 2 and was in hospital 'for a number of days' before he died on November 5. His parents were said to have remained at his side. Referring to brief details of what happened, Ms Kearsley said Thiago was at the nursery on November 2 when there was an 'incident there in which he was found to be choking'. To make sure you can see all of the biggest stories from Greater Manchester and its surrounding areas in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source He was taken to hospital, but sadly died despite medical intervention, the court heard. Ms Kearsely said a CT scan found he had suffered 'an unsurvivable hypoxic brain injury'. The court heard the GMP investigation would 'take months rather than weeks' and no date was set for a full inquest. Ms Kearseley said: "I am sure everybody would wish to express our condolences to Thiago's family'. There were no family members at the hearing. Pictures from the scene at the time showed a large response with three police vehicles, an ambulance and rapid response paramedic car in attendance. The air ambulance was also pictured landing nearby. The Cosy Toes nursery has been closed in the aftermath. Representatives for the nursery described Thiago as a 'wonderful and beautiful child' in the aftermath. A spokesperson for the nursery said: "We are all heartbroken to hear of the tragic news of the child’s passing. "He was a wonderful and beautiful child, and our thoughts and prayers are all with his family at this terrible time. We will of course give our fullest possible assistance in every way possible to the enquiries that must rightly follow this tragic event." Ofsted has suspended the nursery's registration in the wake of the incident, meaning the nursery will be closed for six weeks whilst enquiries are carried out. Ofsted has since confirmed it has also suspended the registrations of three other Middleton nurseries run by Cosy Toes Nursery Ltd. Boarshaw Private Day Nursery, Kirkway Nursery and Twinkle Toes Nursery were removed from the register on 5 November. No further details have been revealed.

candidates.source_summary: A man who murdered his wife and hid her body under a bed for two days has been jailed for 21 years and six months.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who murdered his wife and hid her body under a bed for two days has been jailed for a minimum of 21 years and six months. Kyle Howard, 36, of Tweedale Street, was sentenced today at Manchester Crown Court. Police found the body of Keeley Aspinall, 44, known as Kiki, on May 25 at their flat on the Freehold Estate. Howard told police he had fatally stabbed Keeley two days earlier and was reporting the incident because her body was beginning to smell. When questioned, Howard said that the pair had been drinking and began to argue in the kitchen. Keeley was cooking at the time and had a knife in her hand as the pair began to “tussle”. Howard admitted he had his hands around Keeley’s neck and punched her, but he could not remember exactly how the knife ended up in Keeley’s chest, but he said it “just did”. A Home Office post-mortem exmination found that Keeley had suffered a stab wound to the chest, bruising to her neck consistent with strangulation and various other scratches and bruises on her body. Throughout the investigation, Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team unravelled a pattern of domestic abuse from Howard toward Keeley.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The countdown to Christmas started at the weekend, with thousands of people attending Ignite Fire Festival and the Christmas Lights Switch-On at Rochdale Town Hall. More than 15,000 people enjoyed the event over three evenings, leading up to the Christmas switch-on at the town hall on Sunday. Ignite, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK and organised by Rochdale Development Agency, transformed the square and gardens around the town hall into a trail of fire, lights and entertainment. Immersive night-time trail, ‘BODY’ took visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience was the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite was its north-west premiere. Visitors were taken on a dramatic journey as they walked through the glowing embers of human metabolism - the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience was both entertaining and educational. There was also a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle and a stunning backdrop, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall. ‘Drum Machine’ - the 20-strong drumming collective brought their dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival, performing multiple sets each night. Special effects company BPM SFX’s fire shows wowed the crowds in front of the town hall. Travelling Light Circus and Rochdale’s Skylight Circus Arts returned with ‘Fireflies,’ a multi-sensory show featuring jugglers, fire torch spinning and more as part of the Culture Co-op programme, with residents trained up over the last few weeks, especially for the festival. On Sunday evening, Middleton Arena’s Christmas pantomime star Buttons (Chris Johnson) introduced proceedings on the balcony alongside his co-star Cinderella (Becca Elizabeth-Davies). Cinderella sang two festive solos and the Mayor of Rochdale Councillor Faisal Rana, greeted the audience alongside the Mayoress, followed by Father Christmas and his town hall helpers. Jamie Lynock, general manager at event sponsor The Trade Centre UK was also introduced to the crowds. Other guests included Rochdale’s members of the UK Youth Parliament, Matilda Duffy and Ayan Bhuiyan, alongside the borough’s two children’s champions - Max Baker and Sofia Liow. All four wished everyone a merry Christmas before helping to push the button and turn on the lights across town. Councillor Rana said: ”It was wonderful to see so many people joining us to celebrate the start of the Christmas season. There is something magical about seeing the lights illuminate in front of the magnificent town hall and watching the countdown to Christmas begin.” Lots of visitors took to social media to praise the event with comments including: “amazing”, “great to see so many visitors in town”, “absolutely fabulous, we loved it”, “brilliant show and great food”, “great to see such a big crowd”, “awesome lights” and “an amazing delight for the senses.”

Visitors arriving at BODY, the trail enjoying its north-west premiere at Ignite Fire Festival. Immersive night-time trail, 'BODY' took visitors on a journey through 6 zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience was the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite was its north-west premiere. Visitors were taken on a dramatic journey as they walked through the glowing embers of human metabolism - the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body's functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience was both entertaining and educational. There was also a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle and a stunning backdrop, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall. ‘Drum Machine’ - the 20-strong drumming collective - brought their dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival, performing multiple sets each night. candidates.source_summary: A pioneering football-based project is helping young girls in the borough build confidence, friendships and resilience through the power of sport.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A pioneering football-based project is helping young girls in the borough build confidence, friendships and resilience through the power of sport. Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust and Pennine Care Charity have teamed up with Rochdale AFC Community Trust to deliver a new programme for girls aged six to 11 who are waiting for, or already receiving, support from Rochdale child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS). The free 36-week pilot uses fun football activities to help girls stay active and develop their confidence, social skills and emotional wellbeing in a safe and welcoming environment. The programme was developed following feedback from parents of children receiving support from CAMHS, who highlighted the need for activities to help their children build self-esteem and make friends. The project is funded by the Football Association’s Empower Her Fund, which supports opportunities for women and girls to get involved in football. Sessions are delivered by experienced staff from Rochdale AFC Community Trust. Sixteen girls have taken part so far, with early feedback showing how much they are enjoying the sessions and the opportunities to build confidence and make new friends. Anders Cox, clinical lead at Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CAMHS, run by Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust, said: “Getting active, making friends and feeling part of something can all support young people’s mental health. “This project gives the girls a fun and welcoming environment where they can build their confidence, learn new skills and enjoy being active together.”
